subject: Network boundary mapping and audit-ready segmentation materials
messages:
From: Maya R. <security@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: segmentation mapping and network diagrams for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well — Acme’s security team is preparing for a SIG assessment and we need an audit-ready summary of Redwood’s network boundaries for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically: 

- High-level network diagram(s) showing control plane vs data plane separation for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Tenant isolation model and routing (how traffic is scoped per-tenant, inter-tenant egress controls).
- Evidence artifacts: VPC ACL exports, example firewall rules, and a brief narrative we can include in the SIG questionnaire.

Can you provide these as a single package (diagram + short narrative + attachments) by EOD Friday PST? Also, please indicate which pieces map directly to SIG/CAT questions so we can attach them in the portal.

Thanks — Maya
Maya R.
Security Lead, Acme Corp
security@acme.com

[Attachment: none in original request]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <security@acme.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-10T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: segmentation mapping and network diagrams for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Laura and Ben for the Dedicated/Private specifics and Marissa for the compliance mapping. We will assemble a consolidated packet. High-level plan below: 

1) Deliverables by EOD Friday PST (2026-09-11 23:59 PST):
   - redwood_segmentation_map_v3.pdf (diagram + legend + brief narrative) [attached]
   - vpc_acl_export_20260910.json (example ACLs for a Dedicated VPC) [attached]
   - sig_response_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping diagram/narrative to SIG questions) [attached]

2) Short summary of isolation model (included in the PDF):
   - Control plane: customer metadata and orchestration services live in a logically segregated control plane; control plane endpoints are in a management VPC with restricted egress and strict mTLS between control components. No customer data is stored in the control plane for Private deployments; for Dedicated, we operate per-customer control plane instances when requested.
   - Data plane: model inference workloads run in tenant-bound GPU pools (Dedicated) or customer-managed VPCs (Private). KV caches and transient artifacts remain ephemeral; persistent customer data storage is only within customer-controlled resources or explicitly approved Redwood-managed storage with KMS keys scoped per tenant.
   - Network boundaries: tenant overlay (L3) combined with host-level microsegmentation (security groups/host firewall) to prevent lateral movement across tenants; egress policing via account-level NAT and per-tenant ACLs.

3) Evidence notes: attachments contain ACL exports and a short checklist mapping to SIG sections for network and boundary controls. Where live screenshots were requested we will provide sanitized examples and provide reviewer access to a read-only Drive folder.

Please review the attached artifacts and call out any missing items. Laura/Ben — can you confirm the Dedicated VPC firewall rule example is acceptable as representative?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

[Attachments: redwood_segmentation_map_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); vpc_acl_export_20260910.json (JSON, 80KB); sig_response_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T17:05:00Z
Subject: Final: Network boundary package and SIG mapping (Acme)

Maya — attached is the finalized package tailored for Acme (Dedicated). Summary of what’s included and how to use it in the SIG portal: 

1) redwood_segmentation_map_v3.pdf — Single-page diagram + two zoom panels (control plane, data plane) and short narrative. Callouts:
   - Control plane separation: management VPC annotated, ACLs scoped to Redwood operator ASN and management subnets.
   - Data plane: per-tenant GPU pools, example host firewall rules, ephemeral KV cache lifecycle (TTL and eviction behavior spelled out).

2) vpc_acl_export_20260910.json — Exported from our tooling for the Dedicated example. Contains the exact rule names and pseudo-values (sanitized) and a mapping table to SIG network controls.

3) sig_response_matrix.xlsx — Row-per-SIG-question mapping to artifact and suggested language you can paste into the portal (columns: SIG question id, Redwood artifact, suggested response text).

Operational notes for auditors: 
- Tenant isolation is enforced at both L3 and host-level (security groups + host firewall). The diagram shows a tenant overlay network; the example firewall rules show policy-based egress restrictions.
- For Private (customer VPC/on-prem) deployments, the control plane is reachable only over mutually authenticated tunnels; the diagram includes the TLS trust flow and KMS scoping notes.
- We included a screenshot of the read-only Drive folder and have added acme-security@acme.com as a viewer for any live artifacts you need to inspect.

Next steps:
- Maya: if you want we can whiteboard one page of the SIG portal entries together; Ben and I can join a 30-min slot Mon/Tue.
- Marissa: added a short compliance note (see last tab of the XLSX) that maps these artifacts to the SOC 2 network security control language. If you want a SOC 2-ready narrative instead of the SIG-focused language we can produce one follow-up doc.

Link to package (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Redwood-Segmentation-Drive

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
